chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim bin Mihran, from Talha bin Zayd, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who engages in the eating of the clay so he has participated in (shedding) his own blood'.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical significance of eating clay according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) links the physical act of geophagia to a spiritual and physiological depletion of vitality, suggesting that consuming earth draws out one's life essence. Shia scholars often interpret 'shedding one's own blood' metaphorically as the gradual loss of vital energy or the self-inflicted harm that weakens the body's constitution, serving as a warning against excessive or habitual consumption of earth.
